record.paper_title: Bootstrap Algebraic Multigrid: status report, open problems, and outlook
record.original_question: For least-squares interpolation in bootstrap algebraic multigrid, how can one define appropriate local weights ωκ, and possibly corresponding local equations for computing test vectors, in a general algebraic setting so that a globally smooth test vector is not overemphasized in local regions where it has large residuals?

evidence.quote: The related problem of determining appropriate local weights in the LS definition of interpolation is more complicated and has not been resolved in a general algebraic setting, except for finite element discretizations of elliptic boundary value problems.
The problem of determining local weights is also related to the question of deriving local equations for computing the test vectors, as in spectral AMG [22].

A local procedure for finding weights ωκ in (3.1) – to prevent an emphasize on a globally smooth test vector, that will otherwise be heavily weighted everywhere, in the regions where it has large residuals; such approach will be a generalization of the LSR scheme which is now used concurrently with global weights, see Section 3;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a sparse symmetric positive definite linear system $A x = b$ with $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ on a fine index set $\Omega = \{1,\dots,n\}$. Let $\Omega_c \subset \Omega$ be a chosen set of "coarse" indices and $\Omega_f = \Omega \setminus \Omega_c$ the "fine" indices. For each fine index $i \in \Omega_f$ let $\mathcal{C}_i \subset \Omega_c$ be a prescribed local interpolation neighborhood. A prolongation (interpolation) operator $P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times|\Omega_c|}$ is sought of the form
$$ (P v)_i = v_i \text{ for } i\in\Omega_c, \qquad (P v)_i = \sum_{j\in\mathcal{C}_i} p_{ij}\, v_j \text{ for } i\in\Omega_f. $$

Assume that a finite collection of test vectors $\{x^{(\kappa)}\}_{\kappa=1}^K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ has been generated (e.g.\ by relaxation on $A x = 0$ and bootstrap cycling), each representing an algebraically smooth mode. The least-squares (LS) definition of interpolation chooses the rows $\{p_{ij}\}_{j\in\mathcal{C}_i}$ for each $i\in\Omega_f$ to minimize a weighted residual functional
$$ \mathcal{F}_i(\{p_{ij}\}) \;=\; \sum_{\kappa=1}^K \omega_\kappa^{(i)} \left( x^{(\kappa)}_i - \sum_{j\in\mathcal{C}_i} p_{ij}\, x^{(\kappa)}_j \right)^{\!2}, $$
where $\omega_\kappa^{(i)} \ge 0$ are weights that may depend on the local fine index $i$.

Problem. Provide a purely algebraic prescription, applicable to a general sparse SPD matrix $A$ (not restricted to finite-element discretizations of elliptic boundary value problems), for the local weights $\omega_\kappa^{(i)}$ — and, if needed, a corresponding local linear system whose solutions serve as the test vectors $x^{(\kappa)}$ used in $\mathcal{F}_i$ — with the following property:

If a test vector $x^{(\kappa^*)}$ is globally algebraically smooth (small global Rayleigh quotient $\langle A x^{(\kappa^*)}, x^{(\kappa^*)}\rangle / \langle x^{(\kappa^*)}, x^{(\kappa^*)}\rangle$) but exhibits a large local residual, measured for instance by $\|(A x^{(\kappa^*)})|_{\mathcal{N}_i}\|$ on a local neighborhood $\mathcal{N}_i$ of index $i$, then the weight $\omega_{\kappa^*}^{(i)}$ used at index $i$ is automatically reduced relative to the (possibly large) global weight assigned to $x^{(\kappa^*)}$, so that this mode does not dominate the local LS fit at $i$.

The construction must (a) be defined entirely in terms of the entries of $A$ and the test vectors (no geometric or PDE information), (b) generalize the local-spectral / LSR-type weighting used together with global weights for elliptic finite-element problems, and (c) be compatible, in the sense that the resulting $P$ yields a coarse space on which a two-level method with standard smoothing converges uniformly with respect to $n$ for matrices in a stated algebraic class.

Find such a definition of $\{\omega_\kappa^{(i)}\}$ (and accompanying local equations for the test vectors), or prove that no such definition exists in the stated generality.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of defining purely algebraic local LS weights for bootstrap AMG interpolation is described as unresolved in general algebraic settings, with resolution known only for finite-element discretizations of elliptic problems. Subsequent work, including learning-based local weighted least squares (Wang–Gu–Sun–Xu, J. Comput. Phys. 2023) and rBAMG variants, addresses related sub-optimality of spatially shared weights but does not give a definitive general-purpose algebraic prescription. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Learning-based local weighted least squares for algebraic multigrid method
status_evidence.snippet: The prolongation operator constructed by the LWLS model in BAMG may be sub-optimal because of the spatially shared weights and the incomplete representation of the algebraically smooth error.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2023) work still treats the choice of local LS weights in BAMG as an unresolved sub-optimality, addressing it via learning-based heuristics rather than a closed-form algebraic prescription.

status_evidence.title: Bootstrap AMG
status_evidence.snippet: Bootstrap AMG uses a weighted least squares definition of interpolation based on test vectors computed by bootstrap setup cycles and improved by a multigrid eigensolver.
status_evidence.claim: The LS-based interpolation framework on which the question is posed is established in the BAMG literature, with the local-weight question identified as a remaining issue.

status_evidence.title: Relaxation-corrected bootstrap algebraic multigrid (rBAMG)
status_evidence.snippet: rBAMG modifies the LS process to better capture local behavior of test vectors, indicating that local weighting/local equations remain an active research direction.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent algorithmic refinements continue to target the same local-weighting issue, supporting that a general algebraic resolution is still lacking.
